body.name: Cert
body.construction: On input \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\), return incompatible exactly when either \(a-b<-(1-p)r\) or \(a-b>p(1-r)\), and otherwise return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.  If all input cells are rational and the pair is compatible, also use \((c,d)=(cU,0)\) and \((c,d)=(cL,w11)\).  For each pair compute \(t_{00}=c/w00\), \(t_{01}=(a-c)/w01\), \(t_{10}=(b-c)/w10\), \(t_{11}=d/w11\), \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\), and \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\).  Use response probabilities \(t_{uv}\) when \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) when \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) when \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) when \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Sort the distinct elements of these probabilities together with \(\{0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\), give \(W0=k\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\), take independent binary \(U0,V0\) with zero-probabilities \(p,r\), set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\) for the just-specified response probability \(h\).  Emit the resulting two models \(M\in MC(A,B)\) as lower- and upper-endpoint certificates.
